record.paper_title: Orthogonality Types in Normed Linear Spaces
record.original_question: Let X be a normed space of dimension at least 3. Area orthogonality x ⊥_A y means that either x or y is zero, or the normalized directions ±x/∥x∥ and ±y/∥y∥ cut the unit ball of the plane spanned by x and y into four quadrants of equal area. If area orthogonality is additive in X, what structural conclusion follows? In particular, does additivity force X to be an inner product space, or can a non-inner-product space of dimension at least 3 have additive area orthogonality?

evidence.quote: Question 4.9.31 What happens when area orthogonality is additive in a space whose dimension is at least three?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a real normed linear space with $\dim X \geq 3$. For nonzero vectors $x, y \in X$, let $P = \mathrm{span}\{x, y\}$ and consider the unit ball $B_P = \{z \in P : \|z\| \leq 1\}$ of the two-dimensional subspace $P$, equipped with the Lebesgue area measure inherited from any linear identification $P \cong \mathbb{R}^2$ (the relations below do not depend on the choice of identification). The four rays $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}(\pm x/\|x\|)$ and $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}(\pm y/\|y\|)$ partition $B_P$ into four sectors. Define area orthogonality by declaring $x \perp_A y$ if $x = 0$ or $y = 0$, or if these four sectors all have equal area (equal to $\tfrac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{area}(B_P)$). The relation $\perp_A$ is said to be additive on $X$ if, for all $x, y, z \in X$,
$$x \perp_A y \text{ and } x \perp_A z \implies x \perp_A (y + z).$$

Question: If area orthogonality $\perp_A$ is additive on $X$, must $X$ be an inner product space? Equivalently, does there exist a non-inner-product normed space $X$ with $\dim X \geq 3$ on which $\perp_A$ is additive?
artifact.status_search_result: Area orthogonality was introduced and studied for normed planes, with several characterizations of inner product spaces obtained for two-dimensional spaces. No source located in the search resolves the additivity problem for $\perp_A$ in dimension at least 3; the question is stated as an open problem in survey literature on orthogonality types and no proof or counterexample appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Area orthogonality in normed linear spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces area orthogonality and studies its properties (homogeneity, symmetry, additivity) and characterizations of inner product spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Area orthogonality is a known concept whose additivity has been linked to characterizations of inner product spaces, but resolution in dimension ≥ 3 is not established.

status_evidence.title: Orthogonality in Normed Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of orthogonality types in normed linear spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys treat additivity of various orthogonalities as standard tools for characterizing inner product spaces; the area orthogonality case in higher dimensions is listed among open questions.
